Yes—standard GNNs can do zero-shot link prediction on unseen knowledge graphs if the graph is reified into a fixed representation [1]. In that setup, five textbook GNNs, including GAT and GraphSAGE variants, transfer zero-shot to many inductive link-prediction benchmarks, and the best off-the-shelf GAT matches a dedicated knowledge-graph foundation model [1].

Other papers also show GNN-based link prediction on knowledge graphs, but they are not about the same “unknown graph” setting: one improves scalable training on large KGs [5], and another studies link prediction for uncertain knowledge graphs with added structural priors [10].
